描述_ZN: The Fish Algae Scroll, Qing Dynasty, Guangxu, painted by Cixi, on silk with color, 124 cm in length and 61.5 cm in width.　　This panel is inscribed: "There is a surplus of joy in the deep spring of the sea. The imperial handwriting in the middle of the month of Jia Ping in the first year of the Guangxu era." Inscribed with the white square seal of "Hanyu Cuzhong" and the vermilion square seal of "Li Juzhen", and the vermilion square seal of "Treasures of the Empress Dowager Cixi" in the upper center, and the right side of "Daya Zhai" Zhu long square seal.　　From the title can be seen, this picture was made in the Qing Guangxu A Chen year, that is, 1904, Cixi was 69 years old.　　The Qing Dynasty consorts often amused themselves with painting and calligraphy, thus killing time. Empress Dowager Cixi was particularly fond of this art, and often rewarded her ministers with so-called "imperial" paintings and calligraphy to show her favor, but most of them were actually written by others, and Miao Jiahui was one of them. Miao Jiahui was a native of Kunming, Yunnan Province. She was the main guide and ghostwriter of Cixi's painting activities, serving beside Cixi for more than 20 years, during which she ghostwrote a large number of works for Cixi.　　This picture is painted with swimming fish and algae in light colors and fresh ink, with high painting skills, and is most likely the work of Miao's ghostwriter.
